docs.text: Model card, Hard-time rules engine. Purpose: Remaining life for fixed-limit (HT) components. Inputs: Component history, maintenance schedule. Method: Minimum remaining across applicable FH/EFH/cycles/landings/calendar limits. Outputs: Due date, governing limit. Known limits: No uncertainty interval (deterministic rule, not a statistical model).

docs.text: Model card, Survival model (Weibull AFT). Purpose: Failure risk for on-condition and condition-monitored components. Inputs: Unit-level exposure (FH, hot-climate share, ACM share, lot). Method: lifelines WeibullAFTFitter per part number, parametric bootstrap for intervals. Outputs: Conditional failure probability, FH to threshold with interval, covariate time ratios. Known limits: Covariates only fit with enough events; small fleet-wide event counts limit statistical power for some part numbers.

facts.outputs: Conditional failure probability, FH to threshold with interval, covariate time ratios

docs.text: Model card, Engine trend monitor. Purpose: Engine temperature margin deterioration tracking (EGT margin on the fighter turbofan, ITT margin on the turboprops). Inputs: Per-sortie EGT or ITT margin readings for every installed engine position. Method: Theil-Sen robust slope over trailing 150 EFH since installation, compared with the fleet slopes for the same metric (5th percentile and confidence interval steeper than the fleet median). Outputs: Projected EFH to the margin limit (10 °C EGT, 15 °C ITT). Known limits: Needs at least 100 EFH and 30 readings since installation to produce a stable slope.
docs.title: Model card: Engine trend monitor

docs.text: Model card, Fatigue projection. Purpose: Airframe fatigue index (FI) limit forecasting for every type. Inputs: Sortie mission mix and per-sortie FI consumption (g-loading for the fighter; pressurisation cycles, landings and gust exposure for the transport and airlifter). Method: Trailing 12-month consumption rate, linear projection to FI 100. Outputs: Projected date, life-gain estimate for reducing the type's most fatigue-heavy mission. Known limits: Linear projection; does not model future mission-mix changes beyond the simple what-if shift.
docs.title: Model card: Fatigue projection

docs.text: Model card, Pattern detectors. Purpose: Lot defects, environmental effects, repeat snags, oil precursor. Inputs: Unit exposure, snag register, maintenance records. Method: Binomial rate comparison (Bonferroni-corrected), AFT covariate significance, rolling-window snag/NFF counts. Outputs: Flagged lots, environmental time ratios, repeat-snag list, precursor correlation. Known limits: Statistical power is limited by this fleet's size (16 aircraft); some planted effects are weak at this scale even when real.

docs.text: Fatigue index (FI): Airframe structural fatigue consumed, 0 to 100. 100 equals design fatigue life. Fighters accumulate it from g-loading per FH; transports and airlifters from pressurisation cycles, landings and gust exposure.
docs.title: Fatigue index (FI)

facts.meaning: Airframe structural fatigue consumed, 0 to 100. 100 equals design fatigue life. Fighters accumulate it from g-loading per FH; transports and airlifters from pressurisation cycles, landings and gust exposure.

docs.text: Hard time (HT): Component removed at a fixed limit (FH, cycles, landings or calendar), whichever comes first.
docs.title: Hard time (HT)

facts.meaning: Component removed at a fixed limit (FH, cycles, landings or calendar), whichever comes first.

docs.text: On-condition (OC): Component inspected or checked periodically and replaced when condition requires.
docs.title: On-condition (OC)

facts.meaning: Component inspected or checked periodically and replaced when condition requires.

docs.text: Condition monitoring (CM): No scheduled task; failures are monitored and analysed statistically.
docs.title: Condition monitoring (CM)

facts.meaning: No scheduled task; failures are monitored and analysed statistically.

docs.text: Life-limited part (LLP): Part with a mandatory hard life (for example engine turbine disc).
docs.title: Life-limited part (LLP)

facts.meaning: Part with a mandatory hard life (for example engine turbine disc).

docs.text: Snag: A defect reported against an aircraft, recorded in the snag register.
docs.title: Snag

facts.meaning: A defect reported against an aircraft, recorded in the snag register.

docs.text: Repeat snag: Same defect recurring on the same aircraft within a defined window.
docs.title: Repeat snag

facts.meaning: Same defect recurring on the same aircraft within a defined window.

docs.text: Unscheduled removal: Component removed due to a failure or suspected failure.
docs.title: Unscheduled removal

facts.meaning: Component removed due to a failure or suspected failure.

docs.text: NFF: No fault found: removed unit tests serviceable in the shop.
docs.title: NFF

facts.meaning: No fault found: removed unit tests serviceable in the shop.

docs.text: MTBF / MTBUR: Mean time between failures (confirmed) and mean time between unscheduled removals (includes NFF).
docs.title: MTBF / MTBUR

facts.meaning: Mean time between failures (confirmed) and mean time between unscheduled removals (includes NFF).

docs.text: Phase inspection: Scheduled major inspection every 150 FH. Minor periodic servicing every 50 FH.
docs.title: Phase inspection

facts.meaning: Scheduled major inspection every 150 FH. Minor periodic servicing every 50 FH.

docs.text: EGT margin: Exhaust gas temperature margin below the limit (°C), monitored on the fighter's turbofan. Decreases with engine deterioration.
docs.title: EGT margin

facts.meaning: Exhaust gas temperature margin below the limit (°C), monitored on the fighter's turbofan. Decreases with engine deterioration.

docs.text: ITT margin: Inter-turbine temperature margin below the limit (°C), monitored on each turboprop of the transports and airlifters. Decreases with engine deterioration.
docs.title: ITT margin

facts.meaning: Inter-turbine temperature margin below the limit (°C), monitored on each turboprop of the transports and airlifters. Decreases with engine deterioration.

docs.text: Borescope inspection: Internal visual inspection of engine hot section through access ports.
docs.title: Borescope inspection

facts.meaning: Internal visual inspection of engine hot section through access ports.

docs.text: SOAP: Spectrometric oil analysis programme.
docs.title: SOAP

facts.meaning: Spectrometric oil analysis programme.

docs.text: Cannibalisation: Moving a serviceable part from one aircraft to another.
docs.title: Cannibalisation

facts.meaning: Moving a serviceable part from one aircraft to another.

docs.text: Serviceability: Share of aircraft serviceable (available to fly) over a period.
docs.title: Serviceability

facts.meaning: Share of aircraft serviceable (available to fly) over a period.

docs.text: CAD/PAD: Cartridge and propellant actuated devices (ejection seat pyrotechnics), calendar-life items. Fighter only.
docs.title: CAD/PAD

facts.meaning: Cartridge and propellant actuated devices (ejection seat pyrotechnics), calendar-life items. Fighter only.

docs.text: Task card: Approved maintenance procedure (fictional) with standard man-hours, elapsed time, interval and manual reference. Every recommendation cites one.
docs.title: Task card

facts.meaning: Approved maintenance procedure (fictional) with standard man-hours, elapsed time, interval and manual reference. Every recommendation cites one.

docs.text: Action plan over the next 90 days: 81 tasks across 28 aircraft, 474 man-hours, 22 tasks this week, peak week starting 15 Nov 2026 with 449 man-hours, lowest projected availability 82% in the week of 15 Nov 2026. Method: Each aircraft's next periodic servicing (50 FH) and phase inspection (150 FH) are projected from the FH flown since the last recorded one, at that aircraft's trailing 90-day utilisation rate. A phase inspection also covers the periodic servicing. Planned package lengths are the midpoint of the configured ranges rounded up: 13 days for a phase inspection, 3 days for a periodic servicing. Packages are extended by whole days of bundled work at 16 man-hours per aircraft per day. Each open recommendation's deadline is its due date, or the date its FH margin runs out at the trailing rate, whichever comes first. Each task goes into the earliest scheduled input that starts at least 3 days and 5 FH before its deadline. Tasks of 10 man-hours or more (engine and module changes, gear changes, wiring troubleshooting) only go into a phase inspection. Critical tasks, and tasks that are due now, go into an input that starts before the aircraft flies again. If none is scheduled, a before-next-flight input is opened on the as-of date. If no scheduled input fits the deadline, a dedicated input is planned as late as the safety margin allows, and dedicated tasks on the same aircraft within 7 days are brought forward to share one input. Man-hours come from the approved task card each recommendation cites (remove and install, inspection, troubleshooting, borescope, oil sampling), plus the phase and periodic servicing packages. Deferral risk is the survival model's conditional failure probability for that unit over the FH until the next phase inspection, from the same fitted Weibull AFT parameters. Rule and trend items have no model risk. Availability is the share of aircraft not in any planned input, averaged over each week. Unscheduled failures are not forecast here; the what-if planning screen covers expected unscheduled removals.
